-- A 2-stage pipeline: `fetch` fills stage register s1, `exec` moves s1
-- into s2. Whether it sustains one item per cycle depends only on the
-- schedule. Compare `exec ≫ fetch` with `fetch ≫ exec` in the Simulation
-- pane: count how often `fetch` fires.
xblue module mkPipe2;
  input Bool reset;
  input Bool out_ready;
  Reg#(Bit#(8)) next <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bool)    v1 <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bit#(8)) s1 <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bool)    v2 <- mkReg(0);
  Reg#(Bit#(8)) s2 <- mkReg(0);

  method Bool    out_valid = v2;
  method Bit#(8) out_data  = s2;

  -- stage 2 drains when the consumer takes the item
  rule drain (v2 && out_ready);
    v2 <= False;
  endrule

  -- move s1 into s2 when s2 is (or just became) free
  rule exec (v1 && !v2);
    s2 <= s1 + 100;
    v2 <= True;
    v1 <= False;
  endrule

  -- fill s1 when it is (or just became) free
  rule fetch (!v1);
    s1 <= next;
    next <= next + 1;
    v1 <= True;
  endrule

  rule clear (reset);
    v1 <= False;
    v2 <= False;
    next <= 0;
  endrule

  -- later stages first: each stage sees the slot its successor freed
  -- this cycle. Try `fetch ≫ exec ≫ drain ≫ clear`.
  schedule drain ≫ exec ≫ fetch ≫ clear;
endmodule

-- ---------------------------------------------------------------- reasoning
open XBlue

structure Regs where
  ctr : BitVec 8       -- `next`: the number of the next item
  v1 : BitVec 1
  s1 : BitVec 8
  v2 : BitVec 1
  s2 : BitVec 8

/-- The registers after one clock cycle of the design itself. -/
def step (reset ready : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  let r := (mkPipe2.design.cycle (.cons reset (.cons ready .nil))
              (.cons s.ctr (.cons s.v1 (.cons s.s1 (.cons s.v2 (.cons s.s2 .nil)))))).regs
  ⟨r.get mkPipe2.next, r.get mkPipe2.v1, r.get mkPipe2.s1, r.get mkPipe2.v2, r.get mkPipe2.s2⟩

/-- The cycle as a story, latest stage first: each rule sees the slot the
    rule before it freed. -/
def spec (reset ready : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) : Regs :=
  -- drain: the consumer takes the item in stage 2
  let v2a := if s.v2 = 1#1 ∧ ready = 1#1 then 0#1 else s.v2
  -- exec: move stage 1 into stage 2 when stage 2 is free
  let ex  := s.v1 = 1#1 ∧ v2a = 0#1
  let s2  := if ex then s.s1 + 100#8 else s.s2
  let v2b := if ex then 1#1 else v2a
  let v1a := if ex then 0#1 else s.v1
  -- fetch: fill stage 1 when it is free
  let fe  := v1a = 0#1
  let s1  := if fe then s.ctr else s.s1
  let ctr := if fe then s.ctr + 1#8 else s.ctr
  let v1b := if fe then 1#1 else v1a
  -- clear
  ⟨if reset = 1#1 then 0#8 else ctr, if reset = 1#1 then 0#1 else v1b, s1,
    if reset = 1#1 then 0#1 else v2b, s2⟩

theorem step_eq_spec (reset ready : BitVec 1) (s : Regs) :
    step reset ready s = spec reset ready s := by
  obtain ⟨c, v1, s1, v2, s2⟩ := s
  simp [step, spec, mkPipe2.design, Design.cycle, mkPipe2.schedule, mkPipe2.interfaces,
    mkPipe2.rules.drain, mkPipe2.rules.exec, mkPipe2.rules.fetch, mkPipe2.rules.clear,
    mkPipe2.signature, Sched.run, Action.step, Action.fires, writesIf, State.write, State.cur,
    State.read, HList.set, HList.get, Expr.eval, Expr.binVal, Common.putR,
    Common.putW, Common.memAt, mkPipe2.next, mkPipe2.v1, mkPipe2.s1, mkPipe2.v2, mkPipe2.s2,
    mkPipe2.reset, mkPipe2.out_ready]
  have bit : ∀ v : BitVec 1, v = 0#1 ∨ v = 1#1 := by decide
  rcases bit reset with rfl | rfl <;> rcases bit ready with rfl | rfl <;>
    rcases bit v1 with rfl | rfl <;> rcases bit v2 with rfl | rfl <;> simp

-- Consequences, each read off the story.

/-- Full speed: with both stages full and a ready consumer, every stage moves
    at once, and the pipeline is full again. One item leaves per cycle. -/
theorem full_speed (c s1 s2 : BitVec 8) :
    step 0#1 1#1 ⟨c, 1#1, s1, 1#1, s2⟩ = ⟨c + 1#8, 1#1, c, 1#1, s1 + 100#8⟩ := by
  rw [step_eq_spec]; simp [spec]

/-- No bubbles: whenever the consumer is ready, a new item is fetched. -/
theorem fetches_every_cycle (ready : BitVec 1) (h : ready = 1#1) (s : Regs) :
    (step 0#1 ready s).ctr = s.ctr + 1#8 := by
  rw [step_eq_spec]; subst h
  obtain ⟨c, v1, s1, v2, s2⟩ := s
  have bit : ∀ v : BitVec 1, v = 0#1 ∨ v = 1#1 := by decide
  rcases bit v1 with rfl | rfl <;> rcases bit v2 with rfl | rfl <;> simp [spec]

/-- Back-pressure with no extra logic: both stages full and the consumer not
    ready, so no guard holds and nothing changes. -/
theorem stalls (c s1 s2 : BitVec 8) :
    step 0#1 0#1 ⟨c, 1#1, s1, 1#1, s2⟩ = ⟨c, 1#1, s1, 1#1, s2⟩ := by
  rw [step_eq_spec]; simp [spec]

explain: The story is the same three rules in the other order. step_eq_spec goes through, and the three throughput theorems are gone: full_speed is false (from a full pipeline, fetch and exec are blocked and only drain moves). What is true is consumer_sees_nothing: when the consumer is ready, drain runs last, so an item is fetched, moved to stage 2 and taken in one cycle, and v2 is already clear at the end of every cycle. out_valid, which the interfaces rule reads at the start of the cycle, stays 0 while items stream through and are consumed unseen. fetch fires just as often (26 of 32 cycles in both traces), but the registers no longer separate the stages. With later stages first, each item spends a cycle in each register, and the consumer sees every item.
